title: Circling in on plasmids: benchmarking plasmid detection and reconstruction tools for short-read data from diverse species
citation: Teixeira et al. 2025, Briefings in Bioinformatics, doi 10.1093/bib/bbaf589
licence: MIT (analysis repository data file); article open access
what_it_is: The published contig-level calls of 13 tools on 250 isolates (12,795 short-read contigs) beside the hybrid-assembly ground truth. Per-isolate precision, recall and F1 are computed by PlasBench from those published calls (plasmid is positive; chromosome, unknown, unclassified and repeat calls count as not plasmid), by contig count and weighted by contig length.

tool_map_notes.PlasmidFinder: A replicon marker, not a classifier; PlasBench scores a replicon baseline instead.

metrics.label: Contig precision (by contig count)
metrics.note: Both score contigs of the short-read assembly against a hybrid truth. PlasBench drops contigs under CONTIG_MIN_LENGTH and labels ambiguous and chimeric contigs unscorable; the published table keeps every contig.

caveats: The published truth is a hybrid assembly built on the same Illumina reads used as benchmark input; 45 of 250 hybrids are not complete (see teixeira2025_repo_ground_truth_summary.tsv).

The published contigs come from the authors' own assembly of each isolate; a PlasBench run assembles the reads again, so contig sets differ and per-isolate numbers are compared as means, not contig by contig.
PlasBench's tool versions and databases differ from the paper's; a gap can be a version effect.
Most of the 250 isolates have no deposited complete assembly: running them in PlasBench needs a hybrid truth rebuilt from the deposited reads (python/build_hybrid_truth.py).
The precision, recall and F1 here are computed from the published calls under the definition above; they are not the figures printed in the paper.
